headline: ISTQB clarifies AI certifications: CT-AI v2.0 for testing AI, CT-GenAI for testing with AI
summary: ISTQB's updated CT-AI v2.0 focuses on testing AI systems, while CT-GenAI teaches how to use generative AI for testing. Choosing the right path depends on whether you test AI or test with AI.
details: ISTQB offers two distinct certifications for AI in testing: CT-AI (AI Testing) and CT-GenAI (Testing with Generative AI). CT-AI v2.0, released April 17, 2026, focuses on testing AI-based systems, while CT-GenAI v1.1, approved July 25, 2025, covers using generative AI for testing.

CT-AI is designed for testers whose products incorporate AI, such as recommendation engines or LLM-based chatbots. It addresses questions of reliability, fairness, and robustness of AI systems themselves. The v2.0 syllabus reduced chapters from 11 to 7 and training from four to three days.

CT-GenAI targets testers who want to integrate generative AI into their workflow for tasks like writing test cases, generating data, or analyzing results. This certification focuses on effective and responsible use of AI assistants without compromising test quality. Prompt engineering is a core component, accounting for 365 of 815 training minutes.

Both certifications require the Certified Tester Foundation Level (CTFL) as a prerequisite. Each exam consists of 40 questions in 60 minutes, with CT-AI v2.0 needing 29/44 points to pass and CT-GenAI requiring 30/46 points.

To choose, start with CTFL. Then, opt for CT-GenAI if your goal is daily productivity with AI assistants, or CT-AI if you are involved in testing products that embed machine learning or language models. The two certifications can also complement each other.
caption:
Are you testing AI systems or using AI to test? ISTQB has two distinct certifications for AI in testing, and knowing the difference is key.

ISTQB offers two distinct certifications for AI in testing: CT-AI (AI Testing) and CT-GenAI (Testing with Generative AI). CT-AI v2.0, released April 17, 2026, focuses on testing AI-based systems, while CT-GenAI v1.1, approved July 25, 2025, covers using generative AI for testing.

CT-AI is designed for testers whose products incorporate AI, such as recommendation engines or LLM-based chatbots. It addresses questions of reliability, fairness, and robustness of AI systems themselves. The v2.0 syllabus reduced chapters from 11 to 7 and training from four to three days.

CT-GenAI targets testers who want to integrate generative AI into their workflow for tasks like writing test cases, generating data, or analyzing results. This certification focuses on effective and responsible use of AI assistants without compromising test quality. Prompt engineering is a core component, accounting for 365 of 815 training minutes.

Both certifications require the Certified Tester Foundation Level (CTFL) as a prerequisite. Each exam consists of 40 questions in 60 minutes, with CT-AI v2.0 needing 29/44 points to pass and CT-GenAI requiring 30/46 points.

To choose, start with CTFL. Then, opt for CT-GenAI if your goal is daily productivity with AI assistants, or CT-AI if you are involved in testing products that embed machine learning or language models. The two certifications can also complement each other.
